Nemotron Bolt will run on both cards with the layers split by bytes, like Kolibri. Before anyone writes its planner I want to understand the generic pieces: how pp_balance in src/runtime/pipeline_plan.h chooses the split, and whether the per-device budget in src/runtime/memory_plan.h already subtracts the driver reserve. Then make the tie rule of pp_balance explicit in its comment (which split wins when two are equally good) and run the pipeline planner's test.

00135| // `pp_no_prefill()` (the default everywhere) is spec 16b's decode-only plan, unchanged.
00136| inline PrefillPath pp_no_prefill() {

00138|   p.prefill = false;
00139|   return p;
00140| }

00144| //   mtp   the MTP head on the last device (spec 16 §3.1): its weights (PpWeights::mtp) and
00145| //         a REPLICA of the embedding (the operator's choice, as 16b's placement anticipated:

messages.reasoning_content: The comment says the heavier side is minimised, ties to the more even split, then the smaller s. The definition is not in the header; find where it lives and who calls it.
Now the budget side: memory_plan.h decides what a device may hold. The question is whether the reserve is taken off before the planner compares the two sides.
